terminal.description: A shell in your workspace: node run.mjs <file> runs a query file against a fresh copy of the bakehouse database.

tasks.title: Count orders by status
tasks.description:
Odile starts each Monday by asking how many orders are pending, delivered and cancelled.

In `queries/1-status-counts.sql`, return one row per order status with two columns:

- `status`
- `orders`: how many orders have that status

Row order does not matter. The check compares your rows with the expected rows on the shipped data and on a hidden dataset.
nextSteps: Run `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders;` to see the total.
Group the orders so you get one row per status.
Name the count column and run the file.
hints: COUNT(*) counts rows. On its own it counts the whole table.
GROUP BY splits the rows into groups that share a value, and COUNT then counts each group.
Select the column you group by next to COUNT(*), and give the count the name the task asks for with AS.

tasks.title: Summarize prices by category
tasks.description:
Tobias is reviewing prices and wants one line per product category.

In `queries/2-category-prices.sql`, return one row per `category`, sorted by category from A to Z, with these columns in any order:

- `category`
- `products`: how many products are in it
- `cheapest`: the lowest price
- `dearest`: the highest price
- `avg_price`: the average price, rounded to 2 decimal places with `ROUND(value, 2)`

The check compares rows and their order on the shipped data and on a hidden dataset.
nextSteps: Group the products by category and count them.
Add the lowest and highest price.
Add the rounded average and the sort.
hints: MIN, MAX and AVG work like COUNT: one value per group.
You can wrap an aggregate in another function, for example ROUND(AVG(price), 2).
Every column in the SELECT list is either the grouped column or an aggregate. Then add ORDER BY category at the end.

tasks.title: Find the regular cafes
tasks.description:
Odile wants to thank the cafes that keep coming back. A regular is a cafe with at least 3 **delivered** orders. Cancelled and pending orders do not count.

In `queries/3-regular-cafes.sql`, return:

- `cafe_id`
- `delivered`: how many delivered orders that cafe has

Only cafes with 3 or more delivered orders. Sort by `delivered` from most to fewest, then by `cafe_id` from smallest to largest.

The check compares rows and their order on the shipped data and on a hidden dataset.
nextSteps: Count orders per cafe and look at the numbers.
Decide which rows to remove before grouping and which groups to remove after.
Add the sort and compare a few counts by hand.
hints: Two different filters are needed: one about single orders and one about whole groups.
WHERE removes rows before they are grouped. HAVING removes groups after they are counted.
Filter the status in WHERE, group by cafe_id, keep groups with HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3, then ORDER BY two columns.
